source_concerns: Source VII_A 8.4 reference label is sga3:xv:definition:8-4; preserved but apparent target mismatch requires reference audit.

Lemma 2.5 proof calls q the order of torsion subgroup, then claims q-power torsion subgroups are schematically dense (fails for q=1), and says finite diagonalizable groups are completely split coverings without stated root-of-unity base change. Faithfully preserved; French verification required.
Theorem 2.1 permits q>0 including q=1; likely source defect; no mathematical alteration made.
Footnote citing BIBLE 4.6 is linked to sga3:xv:lemma:4:6 in the English source; retained pending reference audit.
Proof §2.2(b) cites III 4.6 using own xv:lemma4:6 key; retained pending reference audit.

Proof §2.2(c) says vanishing in every residue-field fibre suffices for a section of a coherent sheaf to vanish, which fails on nonreduced bases without additional argument; verify French and mathematical meaning.
Lemma 2.9 TDTE IV Lemma 3.6 links to own xv:lemma3:6; preserved pending source reference audit.
Lemma 2.10 proof says {}_n T_0 is flat over S, though defined over closed S_0; expected S_0. Preserved awaiting French verification.
Proof §3.2 VI_B 5.2 reference uses own xv:theorem5-2 key in source. Preserved.
Remarks 3.5 item (2) is hyperlinked to xv:theorem5:2 by source; preserved.
Lemma 3.7 proof refers to u_0 as a morphism but then says its inverse image extends to an isomorphism; expected chosen u_0 to be an isomorphism. Preserved.
English trivial torus/group in §3.3 means split (as shown by Tprime=G_m^r), rendered 分裂 to avoid claiming rank-zero torus.
